items.category: 考古 · 牙齿里的线索
items.headline: 广西洞穴里的牙齿，为什么指向雨林？
items.headline_en: Fossil Teeth Point to an Ancient Rainforest
items.summary: 11 月 18 日发表的两项研究分析了广西两座洞穴出土的化石。牙釉质保留了食物和饮水留下的化学线索，直立人与同地动物的牙齿都指向热带雨林。测年结果表明，约 32 万至 18 万年前，直立人已能在这里的密林中生活。
items.summary_en: Two studies published on 18 November examined fossils from two caves in Guangxi. Tooth enamel preserves chemical clues from food and water. Teeth from Homo erectus and local animals both point to a rainforest, where these ancient humans were able to live roughly 320,000 to 180,000 years ago.

items.headline: 没有星空，迁徙的飞蛾怎么找方向？
items.headline_en: How Do Moths Navigate Without Stars?
items.summary: 11 月 18 日发表的实验发现，澳洲博贡蛾不仅靠星空辨向，也能感知地磁。研究人员用线圈改变磁场，飞蛾随之改变飞行方向。它感知的线索之一是磁场与地面的夹角，这不同于普通指南针指向磁北的方式。
items.summary_en: In a study published on 18 November, Australian Bogong moths changed their heading when researchers altered the magnetic field with coils. The moths use stars as well as a magnetic cue: the tilt of Earth’s field relative to the ground. That is different from a compass needle pointing towards magnetic north.

items.headline: 一颗恒星怎样落进另一颗恒星？
items.headline_en: How Does One Star Spiral Into Another?
items.summary: NASA 11 月 18 日介绍了仙女座星系的一次恒星合并。伴星进入巨星的外层气体后，阻力使它失去轨道能量，向内越绕越近。研究者把爆发前后的观测拼在一起，发现这两颗恒星从接触到合并只绕了约七圈。
items.summary_en: On 18 November, NASA reported on a stellar merger in Andromeda. Once the smaller star entered the giant’s outer gas, drag drained its orbital energy and sent it spiralling inward. Observations before and after the eruption show that the stars completed only about seven orbits between contact and merger.

items.headline: 咖啡渣做成的炭，能抓住水里的什么？
items.headline_en: What Can Carbon Made from Coffee Grounds Trap?
items.summary: 11 月 15 日发表的实验把废咖啡渣制成多孔活性炭，用两种处理方法改变它的表面。水中的头孢氨苄分子可以附着在孔壁上；在同一测试条件下，两种材料分别去除了约 88% 和 70%。吸附是把分子留在炭表面，不是把它分解。
items.summary_en: A study published on 15 November turned used coffee grounds into porous activated carbon using two treatments. Molecules of the antibiotic cephalexin adhered to the pore walls. Under the same test conditions, the two materials removed about 88% and 70%, respectively. Adsorption traps the molecules on a surface rather than breaking them down.

items.headline: 哪片灌木可能把火带上树冠？
items.headline_en: Where Can Shrubs Carry a Fire Into the Canopy?
items.summary: NASA 11 月 18 日介绍了加州的激光雷达地图。飞机发出的激光脉冲从树冠、灌木和地面反射回来，往返时间能换算成距离。用这些数据画出植被的高度和层次，就能找出哪些地方的灌木可能把地面火带上树冠。
items.summary_en: On 18 November, NASA highlighted California’s lidar maps. Laser pulses from an aircraft bounce off treetops, shrubs and the ground. Their travel times give distances. Mapping these layers helps identify where shrubs could carry a ground fire up into the canopy.

items.headline: 看起来四季常绿的雨林，也会成片落叶吗？
items.headline_en: Can an Evergreen-Looking Rainforest Lose Its Leaves?
items.summary: 11 月 18 日发表的研究用 10 米分辨率的卫星影像追踪亚马孙森林。大片森林从远处看终年是绿的，细看却能发现，不少斑块会在一年中的某段时间落叶，时间和程度各不相同。把整片雨林当成全年不变的绿盖，会漏掉这些变化。
items.summary_en: A study published on 18 November tracked Amazon forest cover using satellite images at 10-metre resolution. The forest can look green year-round from afar, yet many patches shed leaves seasonally, with different timing and intensity. Treating the whole forest as uniformly evergreen misses those changes.

previous_answers.headline: 选一个三位数，要求百位与个位相差至少2。把它的数字顺序倒过来，用较大的数减去较小的数。再把所得差的数字顺序倒过来，将这两个数相加。不必知道最初选的数，你能预测最后的结果吗？说明理由。（倒序后开头的0可以略去。）
previous_answers.headline_en: Choose a three-digit number whose first and last digits differ by at least 2. Reverse its digits, then subtract the smaller number from the larger. Reverse the digits of the difference and add these two numbers. Can you predict the final total without knowing the starting number? Explain why. Any leading zero in a reversed number may be omitted.
previous_answers.explanation: 设首尾数字之差为 d，则减出的数是 99d，三位数字依次为 d−1、9、10−d。倒序相加时，两端各凑成 9，中间相加得 18；进位后就是 1089。
previous_answers.explanation_en: Let d be the difference between the first and last digits. Subtracting gives 99d, whose digits are d−1, 9 and 10−d. Adding its reversal gives 9 at both ends and 18 in the middle before carrying, which gives 1,089.

previous_answers.headline: 12张卡片分别写着1至12。充分洗匀后，随机抽出3张，不放回。三张卡片上的数之和能被3整除的概率是多少？请用清楚的分类计数说明答案，而不是只靠模拟。
previous_answers.headline_en: Twelve cards are numbered 1 to 12. Shuffle them thoroughly and draw three without replacement. What is the probability that their sum is divisible by 3? Explain your answer by counting cases, rather than relying only on a simulation.
previous_answers.explanation: 按除以 3 的余数分三类，每类 4 张。要使和整除，三张的余数要么全相同，要么各不相同。符合的组合有 3×4＋4³＝76 种；一共 220 种，所以是 76/220＝19/55。
previous_answers.explanation_en: There are four cards in each remainder class modulo 3. For the sum to be divisible by 3, the remainders must be all equal or all different. This gives 3×4 + 4³ = 76 valid triples out of 220, so the probability is 19/55.

previous_answers.headline: 7名选手进行单循环比赛：每两人恰好比赛一场，每场都有一名胜者，没有平局。证明：无论比赛结果如何，总能把7人排成一列，使每个人都赢过紧挨在自己后面的人。注意：不要求一个人赢过自己后面的所有人。
previous_answers.headline_en: Seven players compete in a round-robin tournament: every pair plays exactly once, and every match has one winner, with no draws. Prove that, whatever the results, the players can always be arranged in a line so that each player beat the person immediately after them. A player need not have beaten everyone farther down the line.
previous_answers.explanation: 先排一人，再逐个加入。新选手若谁也没赢过，就放在末尾；否则把他插到队中第一位被他打败的人前面。若前面还有一人，那人一定赢过新选手，所以两个新的相邻关系都成立。
previous_answers.explanation_en: Start with one player and add the rest one at a time. If the newcomer beat nobody in the line, put them at the end. Otherwise, insert them just before the first player they beat. Any player immediately before that position must have beaten the newcomer, so both new links work.
previous_answers.subject: W46 · 胜者队列解答

challenges.headline_en: Three opaque boxes contain two red balls, two blue balls, and one of each, respectively. The three labels, “two red”, “two blue” and “one of each”, are all wrong. You may choose one box and draw one ball without looking inside. How can you identify the contents of all three boxes?
